components.summary: Three-dot waiting animation — "something is being produced" (a streaming reply, a model loading), where .df-spinner means "a request is in flight".

attributes.name: variant
attributes.notes: flash (one light runs left-right-back), fade (dots fade in turn), wave (dots hop in turn), pulse (each dot swells in turn). Empty picks one at random per instance.

attributes.name: look
attributes.notes: smooth: 6px dots, 28px wide, 1em tall — sits inline next to text and animates transform/opacity only, so it stays smooth while a stream repaints the page. classic: 10px dots, 50px wide, box-shadow animation — the larger, livelier one for an empty bubble.

consumes_css_vars.affects: the lit dot (classic) and every dot (smooth); defaults to --accent
the resting dots in classic (smooth rests at a lower opacity instead); defaults to --border-strong

components.a11y: role=status with aria-label="waiting". prefers-reduced-motion stops the animation and leaves resting dots.
gotchas: look=classic draws wave and pulse 20px above its own box and needs about 25px of room above the baseline — give it a block of its own, not a line of text.

components.summary: Anchored panel primitive: hangs arbitrary content off a trigger in the top layer, with light-dismiss and same-trigger toggle.

slots.name: trigger
slots.purpose: The anchor element; clicking it toggles the panel.

consumes_css_vars.affects: panel border color (override for a quiet-at-rest / accent-when-open trigger)

components.a11y: Panel is role=dialog; light-dismiss on outside-click and Esc (scroll never dismisses); same-trigger click toggles.
gotchas: placement splits on '-': base edge (top|bottom|left|right) + align (start|end). bottom-start aligns the panel's LEFT edge to the trigger; bottom-end aligns its RIGHT edge. Bare 'left'/'right' default to -start.
Panel is position:fixed in the top layer (native popover), so it escapes overflow/scroll clipping.
Tracks the trigger on scroll and resize (capture-phase scroll listener catches inner scroll containers too); it repositions rather than dismissing.

It aligns to the border-box of whatever you put in slot=trigger. A druid-button's inner <button> sizes to its content and won't fill a forced-wider host width, so give the trigger its natural size or the alignment will look offset.
Flips to the opposite side when short on viewport space, then clamps into the viewport.
Placement is druids.anchor(); use that directly to build an overlay control of your own that must escape a clipping ancestor.

components.summary: framework-styled dropdown (native <select> popups are OS-rendered and can't match the design).

attributes.name: value
attributes.notes: Also a live property: read `.value` for the current selection, assign it to select programmatically (no `change` fires for a programmatic set). A value matching no option shows the placeholder — unless `free` is set, which shows the raw value.

attributes.name: filter
attributes.notes: Adds a filter box on top of the menu: case-insensitive match on label and value, prefix matches first, at most 100 rows rendered (a note counts the rest). Arrow keys move the highlight, Enter picks it.

attributes.name: free
attributes.notes: With `filter`: Enter commits the typed text even when it matches no option (an exact match is still picked as that option).

components.a11y: Trigger is aria-haspopup=listbox with aria-expanded; menu is role=listbox, items role=option.
components.example:
<druid-select name="model" placeholder="Choose model">
  <option value="a">Model A</option>
  <option value="b">Model B</option>
</druid-select>
gotchas: Set `name` to get a hidden light-DOM input so classic form POSTs carry the value.
Options are declared as <option> children, never rendered directly; they are watched via MutationObserver.

<druid-select> is not a labelable element, so a wrapping <label> associates with nothing (label.control is null). Use a <div class="df-field"> with a <span class="df-label">, and set label="…" on the select — it becomes the trigger's aria-label.

The menu renders in the top layer (native popover, placed by druids.anchor()), so an overflow:auto or overflow:hidden ancestor — a scrolling table, a .df-dialog, a .df-card — cannot clip it. It is display:none when closed, so it never inflates the scroll height of its container. Scrolling repositions the menu rather than closing it.

Narrow hosts: the select shrinks with its container and ellipsizes the label (130px is a floor only when there is room); the menu is capped at the viewport width and ellipsizes long options, with the full text in each row's title.
Keyboard: ArrowDown opens the closed select; while open, arrows move the highlight, Enter picks it, Esc / Tab close.

components.summary: Sorting and live filtering for a plain light-DOM table (slotted, never rebuilt).

attributes.name: filter
attributes.notes: the active query; set it from the app to filter without the built-in box.

attributes.name: sort
attributes.notes: column key to sort by: a <th>'s data-key, else its trimmed header text.

detail.key: string — the sorted column's data-key, else its header text

consumes_css_vars.affects: header bar of the boxed table

components.a11y: Sorted headers carry aria-sort=ascending|descending; the filter input is labelled from search-placeholder.
components.example:
NameSizeActions
gemma8.1 GBrun
gotchas: The table is slotted light DOM: style it with .df-table and render its rows server-side as usual. The component only reorders <tr> nodes and toggles their hidden flag.
Sorting compares a cell's data-value when present, else its text; two values that both parse as numbers compare numerically. Use data-value for anything formatted ("8.1 GB", a date).
<th data-sort="none"> opts a column out of sorting (action columns).
Rows added or replaced later are picked up automatically by a MutationObserver; call refresh() only if you mutate rows in a way that does not touch the DOM.
Sticky headers and the scroll container come from .df-table / .df-table-wrap in druids.css, not from this component.

A .df-table is width:100%, so it can never outgrow the scroll container and a narrow viewport squeezes the columns. Add class "wide" to the table (or tune --df-table-min-width) to give it a width floor and get horizontal scrolling; tables with 5+ columns get that floor automatically under 720px.

The scroll container only engages if the table's ancestors can shrink: give any grid track minmax(0, ...) and any flex/grid item min-width: 0, otherwise the ancestor grows to the table's floor and the page gets the horizontal scrollbar instead. Applies to the automatic 5+-column floor too, which needs no opt-in.

components.summary: The strip scrolls inside itself instead of widening the page: min-width 0 lets it shrink below its content.
components.a11y: Document-level tab strip; you own the .df-tab-panel[data-tab-panel] sections and toggle .active.
components.example:
<druid-tabs active="home">
  <druid-tab panel="home">Home</druid-tab>
  <druid-tab panel="logs">Logs</druid-tab>
</druid-tabs>
<section class="df-tab-panel active" data-tab-panel="home">…</section>
gotchas: The strip scrolls horizontally inside itself when the tabs do not fit, so it never widens the page on a narrow viewport — in the navbar or placed in content alike.

components.summary: a textarea whose default height is set in line counts.
gotchas: Light DOM, so it posts in normal forms and autofills. maxlength -1 = no limit; autosize grows to content.

components.summary: Themed hover/focus bubble that wraps the element it describes; works over disabled controls where native title is unreliable.

slots.purpose: The element being described (the hover/focus target).

components.a11y: Bubble is role=tooltip; shows on hover and focus-within, Esc hides it.
components.example:
<druid-tooltip text="Locked while a model is pinned">
  <druid-textarea disabled></druid-textarea>
</druid-tooltip>
gotchas: Empty or cleared `text` hides the bubble entirely — drive a conditional tooltip by setting/clearing `text` (or set `disabled`).
Bubble renders in the top layer, so scroll/overflow ancestors never clip it; it flips to stay on-screen.
Because the wrapper owns the hover, it fires over a disabled child control (unlike native title).

The top layer is the top layer of the tooltip's own document: inside a tiny iframe (a 40px extension toolbar) the bubble has nowhere to go and covers its neighbours. There, rely on the native title the control's `label` already sets — the browser draws that outside the frame.

apis.summary: Array of preset accent hex values (the palette).

apis.signature: anchor(panel: HTMLElement, target: Element, opts: AnchorOptions = {}): AnchorHandle
apis.summary: Place a panel against an anchor element: position:fixed, flips when short of room, clamped and width-capped to the viewport, follows the anchor on scroll/resize; a panel with the `popover` attribute is also lifted into the top layer. The primitive behind druid-popover and druid-select — use it for an overlay control of your own that must escape a .df-card (overflow: hidden) or a transformed ancestor. Returns { update(), release() }.
Set the app accent color (hex); persisted per app.
Tint the neutral surfaces with a palette hue, by swatch name (or "neutral" for a grey base). Unknown names are ignored; this only paints — <druid-flavor-picker> also persists.
Drop the flavor overrides so druids.css owns the surfaces again (the stock blue-grey).
Promise-returning yes/no modal on the .df-dialog chrome. Resolves false on cancel or dismiss.
apis.example: druids.confirm("Delete this model?", { danger: true }).then(ok => { if (ok) … });

apis.summary: Array of flavor hue names, in palette order (the accent swatch names).

apis.signature: form(message: string, opts: FormOptions): Promise<Record<string, FormValue> | null>
apis.summary: Promise-returning multi-field dialog — prompt() for more than one input. Resolves an object keyed by field `name` (number fields resolve numbers, or null when left blank; checkboxes booleans; everything else strings), or null on cancel/dismiss. `required`, the control's own constraints (min/max/step, type=email/url) and a per-field `validate` returning a message hold the dialog open and tint the field.
Open a modal with arbitrary content on the .df-dialog chrome (backdrop / Esc / focus-trap); returns the <dialog>, already open.
apis.example: druids.modal({ title: "Repo quants", content: node, actions: [{ label: "Close" }] });

apis.signature: prompt(message: string, opts: PromptOptions = {}): Promise<string | null>
apis.summary: Promise-returning text-input modal. Resolves the string on OK, or null on cancel/dismiss.
apis.example: druids.prompt("Pin as:", { value: current }).then(name => { if (name !== null) … });

apis.summary: Register one icon by name for <druid-icon> / icon=.
Register a map of {name: svgString} for <druid-icon> / icon=.
